title: ep0ch-door + pi-herdr-outliner: the architecture map
about: Every structure in the two repos, where it stands on the ladder, what it rests on and what is still open. Regenerated after each round of changes with `bun scripts/architecture-map.ts`; the generator checks every file:line below against the checkouts before it draws anything.

ladder.about: it exists because something needed it; nobody owns it as a system
named as a system, with one owner, but not yet shaped as one
shaped as a system, used by one or two hosts; its contract can still move
one implementation that several hosts or clients use
a contract others build on; changes are additive

chapters.title: The outline and the service
chapters.lede: Everything starts as blocks in one SQLite file per outline, owned by one service process. Blocks have revisions and provenance; properties are [key::value] tokens in the text, read by one grammar.

chapters.title: Capabilities and the change feed
chapters.lede: Clients ask `ping` what the service can do and pick features by capability, not by protocol bumps. Every committed change is a numbered record: live on `events.subscribe`, replayable from `changes.since`.

chapters.title: The socket
chapters.lede: The door speaks to the service over its Unix socket through one client, SocketBoard. Where a call per paint is too slow, the door holds a copy of the service's grammar, checked byte for byte; the older mirrors are still here.

chapters.title: NoteSurface
chapters.lede: One reader draws every note in the door: the board's preview and details, the desk's readers, the river's columns, the BBS message reader and the hub screens. Editing is one draft component under all of them.

chapters.title: The action registry
chapters.lede: An action is an ActionDef in an ActionSet: typed arguments, an actor, a refusal with a reason. Every screen runs its keys and clicks through it: a screen spec's key map names actions, and one dispatcher per screen host runs them (PIE-514). ActionDef.keys is the caption.

chapters.title: The layout tree and tiles
chapters.lede: The desk is a tree of splits, tab sets and tiles, each with a stable id, and a revision any agent can check with expected=. The algebra is pure and shared; the host around it is still the desk's own.

chapters.title: Terminal tiles and Herdr
chapters.lede: A tile can run a program: a pty from Bun, the screen through @xterm/headless. An agent that must outlive the door runs in a Herdr pane the tile attaches to. Every exit goes through one teardown.

chapters.title: Screens as specs
chapters.lede: Every screen is a spec on the one screen host, the desk: containers and tiles by kind, a key map naming actions, a hint, a band, where opens land, all plain data. The desk, the welcome, the brief, Waiting, a pinned page, the board (its lanes a hub source's columns) and the river (a flow) are specs, and no class extends Desk (PIE-515); the BBS screens are outside the tree.

chapters.title: Agents via act and peek
chapters.lede: A second actor drives the door over its control socket: peek and snap to see, act to do, subscribe for the live feed. An agent's action is attributed and never takes the person's focus, selection or keys.

chapters.title: Extensions
chapters.lede: What a third party can add: resource providers and component renderers in the outliner, and, in the door, any program in a terminal tile that drives the door over EP0CH_CONTROL. Tile kinds, keys and screens can't be added yet.

structures.name: SQLite (bun:sqlite)
structures.does: Holds each outline: blocks, properties, the change feed, bookmarks, captures.
structures.built: One database per outline, opened by the store; the kernel releases its write lock when the process dies.

structures.name: Outline store
structures.does: Blocks with revisions and provenance (author, actor). Every write names the revision it read; a stale write is refused.
structures.built: OutlinerStore over SQLite: a blocks table and a block_properties index; update() is the one text write, and properties.patch is an update at an expected revision.

refs.m: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS blocks

structures.name: Workspace ownership lock
structures.does: One service per outline. A crash releases the lock; nothing needs cleaning up.
structures.built: A SQLite write reservation on a lock file beside the database (acquireLockFile). Review B calls it the best runtime code in either repo.

questions.text: `:memory:` stores still create a stray `:memory:.owner.sqlite` in the working directory.

structures.name: Outline host
structures.does: One socket serves several outlines by name (pie, a pilot outline, a sandbox); clients name the outline on each request.
structures.built: OutlineHost answers outlines.list/create/adopt/attach/close/delete/pane and routes every other request to the named outline's server.

questions.text: Folder to outline is still worked out on each client (the door's discover.ts); an `outlines.resolve` on the host would say it once.

structures.name: Property grammar
structures.does: The one definition of a property key and a [key::value] token, with its escape. [2nd-pass::yes] is text; [plot.row::3] is a property.
structures.built: src/property-grammar.ts imports nothing, so a client can copy it whole; properties.ts and block-query.ts build on it; ping reports its version.

structures.name: Query language and saved views
structures.does: A saved view is a block whose query picks other blocks: the board's lanes, Tree's virtual branches. views.read evaluates it; query.expression and query.matches answer ad-hoc questions.
structures.built: block-query.ts parses property filters; the server answers views.read and query.matches from the store. The door's port of this language (query.ts) is deleted.

structures.name: Protocol and capabilities
structures.does: Line-delimited JSON over a Unix socket. The protocol stays at 82; new features are additive capabilities that ping lists, and a client names the one it's missing.
structures.built: OUTLINER_PROTOCOL_VERSION and OUTLINER_CAPABILITIES in types.ts; ping answers them with the grammar version and where the outline lives.

structures.name: Change feed
structures.does: Every committed change is a numbered record (kind, block, parent, revision, actor). Live on events.subscribe; after a reconnect, changes.since replays what was missed.
structures.built: ChangeFeed writes change_feed rows in the same transaction as the change; publishChanges turns each record into an event and broadcasts it to every subscriber.

refs.m: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_feed

structures.name: views.planWrite
structures.does: What moving a block into a saved view would patch, at the block's revision, or why it can't; what a new block there is born with. The service owns the semantics; clients ask.
structures.built: view-writes.ts splits a view's query into clauses a write sets and clauses that must already hold, then evaluates the whole query on the patched block. Ported from the door's move planning, which it replaces.

questions.text: One client so far (the door's board). Tree's virtual branches, the CLI's work_stage and agents could plan through it too.

structures.name: tree.search (Goto)
structures.does: Ranked search over the outline, text or semantic. Goto uses it; the door doesn't.
structures.built: Answered in the server before the request switch; the Goto controller asks it as you type.

questions.text: The door has four searches of its own. One jump palette over tree.search would replace them.

structures.name: Outliner client library
structures.does: The outliner's own client: requests, the watcher on the event feed. Detail, Tree, the CLI and the publisher use it.
structures.built: OutlinerClient and OutlinerWatcher in client.ts.

questions.text: The door has its own client (SocketBoard) beside it: two client libraries for one protocol.

structures.name: Detail
structures.does: The outliner's reader and editor for one block, in a Herdr pane: properties, comments, backlinks, resources.
structures.built: detail-controller and two renderers (pi-tui, ansi); its keys resolve through the outliner keymap by scope.

structures.name: Tree
structures.does: The outline as a tree with virtual branches (saved views), in a Herdr pane.
structures.built: createTreeController with injected effects; rows, layout and mouse in their own modules.

structures.name: SocketBoard
structures.does: The door's one client of the service: requests with timeouts, capabilities, reconnect with backoff, catch-up from changes.since, and 'offline' when it can't ask.
structures.built: One class in socket.ts. The door requires protocol 82 with every capability it names (OUTLINE_CAPABILITIES) and refuses an older service at info(), naming what it lacks and the fix, instead of falling back.

questions.text: The door re-derives the service's state root and socket hash (discover.ts); the host should say.

structures.name: The grammar copy
structures.does: Finds [key::value] tokens at paint time (titles, digests, colour) by the service's own rule, so the door and Detail agree on every note.
structures.built: src/vendor/property-grammar.ts is the outliner's file byte for byte; a test pins its checksum and compares it with the checkout; ping's version is checked at start. It replaced nine local regexes.

structures.name: Grammar mirrors
structures.does: Literal regions, inline Markdown, component renderers, the backlink view and folder-to-outline, drawn the way the outliner draws them.
structures.built: Ports of the outliner's rules, parity-tested against the checkout. components.ts reads the outliner's renderer config on the door's machine, which is wrong for a remote door.

questions.text: Pure paint-time grammar belongs in a module the outliner exports; the component registry and folder-to-outline are host calls.

structures.name: NoteSurface
structures.does: The one reader: render, fold, elements and the ruler, links and history, comments, steps, selection, edit. Hosted by the board, the desk, the river, the BBS reader and the hub screens.
structures.built: NoteSurface behind the SurfaceHost seam; its actions are NOTE_ACTIONS, so a person's key and an agent's act run the same code. staleOn says whether a change makes its note stale (a trash too) and reread reads it again, coalesced: every host asks the surface, none keeps its own rule (#104). What takes its keys besides reading (a status choice, the property panel, the edit, the comment session) is a mode in its ModeStack, precedence stated once (PIE-516).

structures.name: Draft editor
structures.does: Every text the door writes: a note edit, a comment, a reply, a new card. Nested lists, hanging wraps, the mouse, a live preview; its lifecycle (put aside, restore, hold) is the draft session's.
structures.built: Draft in edit.ts and the edit control in surface/editor.ts; its keys and clicks are DRAFT_ACTIONS, forwarded as note actions for act.

structures.name: Draft session
structures.does: One lifecycle for every draft the door writes: open with what was put aside, the service hold, key and leave, written or refused (stale keeps it), put aside as unsent, recordAs. Every rule about an agent and a draft, and the invitation an @name line gives one agent.
structures.built: DraftSession in draft-session.ts behind three target adapters: blockTarget (update a block), commentTarget (a comment or reply, one request id per text), cardTarget (card.create through views.planWrite, or note.create). Hosts (the reader, the comment session, the board's composer) call key and leave (PIE-516).

structures.name: Action registry
structures.does: An action: a name, typed arguments, an actor, a refusal with a reason. The same code for the person's key, a click and an agent's act.
structures.built: ActionDef and ActionSet in surface/actions.ts. ActionDef.keys is a display string: nothing binds a key to an action. Each def declares what it touches of the person's (touches: nothing, tile, shape, draft, screen; person: the person's only) and whether a restarted door may run it again (replay: safe or ask), and what an agent's run says (says) (PIE-514).

questions.text: Keys bind through ActionDefs: a binding table, one keymap, hints and ? generated from it.
Five hand-written act() routers, four ways to name a reader.

structures.name: The dispatcher and the actor rule
structures.does: One door every action goes through, one per screen host: the person's keys and clicks, an agent's act, a tile holding a whole screen. It reads tile= with one grammar, finds the set that owns a name, checks expected=, checks what the action declares it touches against where the person is (once, before it runs), runs it as the person (a refusal said, then a redraw) or as an agent (announced, refused with the reason, what it did said).
structures.built: Dispatcher, TileRef and actorRule in surface/dispatch.ts; screens register their action sets (the desk, the board, the welcome, the brief, Waiting, the river, the BBS screens, the showcase, the App's shell, host layer and extensions). The shell's whereabouts query (whereabouts.ts, App.person) answers where the person's keys and focus are, which tile they type in, whether they're busy, how long idle; it feeds the actor rule, the layout engine's ctx.person and, through the dispatcher, the draft session's draftRule (PIE-514).

questions.text: A restarted door re-applies the replay-safe actions it logged and asks before the rest.

structures.name: Shell and list actions
structures.does: screen.open, screen.back, screen.list on every screen; list.select, list.open, list.read on the BBS lists; screen.shell drops to the person's login shell (the menu's !, the desk's ^W !) and the door comes back where it was, an agent's refused. Esc never logs off; q is back below the menu. An agent can't move the person's screen while they type.
structures.built: SHELL_ACTIONS and LIST_ACTIONS in screens.ts; the menu's letters, Enter and clicks run them; the App's dispatcher holds the shell's set (a screen's own action of the same name first); a move of the person's screen declares touches: screen, and the actor rule guards it (PIE-514).

structures.name: Key dispatch
structures.does: Turns a key into what happens: on every screen, into an action, or into an input state (a prefix, a picker, an edit) that ends in one. test/parity.ts fails when a key or click changes the screen without an action naming that key (#96). Keys are still matched in place, screen by screen.
structures.built: Hundreds of in-place comparisons (422 by a grep for c === / ch(k) === / k.kind === at 07d82c9; 86 in delivery.ts, 47 in the river's old screen), each screen with its own priority order.

questions.text: No keymap: share the outliner's keybindings.json shape, with scopes and collision checks.
Same action, different keys; same key, different things.
Hint rows are hand-written and disagree with the keys.

structures.name: Hit-testing
structures.does: What the mouse is over, turned into a key or an action.
structures.built: Ten private maps. Pointer on the BBS screens is the right shape: a spot sends a key back through key(), so click and key are one path.

questions.text: One hit map instead of ten.
The right button is the left button: context menus from the pane's actions.

structures.name: The terminal
structures.does: Alt screen, SGR mouse with button events, bracketed paste, OSC 52 copy, Kitty graphics where there are any. Over ssh and tmux to a phone, and a Mac terminal that types Option as characters.
structures.built: term.ts turns on 1049, 1002, 1006 and 2004 and decodes keys and mouse into Key events (a KeyDecoder per terminal, a session's clients each their own); a frame goes to a Display, a Painter per terminal (its rows diffed by Rows, its Kitty images, its video mode); each chunk of input is handled, then painted once, and a trackpad's burst of wheel reports scrolls a row each (wheelRows); a macOS Option character is read as its alt key outside text (OPTION_KEYS). What reaches the terminal is printable (text.ts printable and paintable: no raw escapes from a note or a program) and measured in cells (style.ts width; fitHint cuts a hint row to fit and says ? more, #103).

questions.text: OSC 52 and the side buttons depend on tmux settings along the path to the phone.

structures.name: Outliner keymap
structures.does: Per-action, per-scope key bindings in keybindings.json, with collision checks, atomic reload, a ? menu and help text. Tree and Detail use it; the door doesn't.
structures.built: OutlinerActionKeymap: resolve by surface and scopes, helpText, menuItems.

questions.text: The door's key layer takes this file's grammar, plus sequences for ^W.

structures.name: The screen-layout module
structures.does: The reducer of the door's one-way data flow (PIE-513): a screen's layout is one value (tiles in containers: n-ary splits by weight, tab sets, drawers, columns from data, flows; floats above the tree; spines, zoom, links, names, the screen's policy and lock, the revision), and it changes only by apply(state, op, ctx): one layout operation for one actor as one transaction, answering the new state or a refusal with its reason. Every rule is checked inside it: floats have no place in the tree, the nearest policy wins and a lock above locks below, an agent undoes only its own lock and never moves the tile the person types in, the screen is never blank. The flow container is the river's columns: squeezed full, peek, spine around the wide one; opens land in the next column; focus never moves it.
structures.built: screen-layout.ts is the interface (apply, refusal, init, serialize, describe, place, landing); layout.ts (the tree arithmetic) and flow.ts (the flow's squeeze and memory) are inside it and import only Rect and the spine's width. What it doesn't own is said to it: the actor, the person's keys and the tile they type in (ctx.person, a shell-owned query from PIE-514), each tile's facts. Its state is frozen under test, so a caller that writes to it throws. Tested through its interface with no App (test/screen-layout.test.ts, test/flow.test.ts), the round-2 review's B7-B11, C3 and C4 among them.

structures.name: Layout identity
structures.does: Every split (s<n>), tab set (g<n>), drawer (d<n>), columns (c<n>), flow (f<n>) and tile (t<n>) keeps an id through moves and saves; the layout has a revision. An agent's expected=<rev> is refused, with nothing done, when the person changed the layout meanwhile.
structures.built: The ids live on the LNode tree; the screen-layout module gives them and moves the revision on a change of shape, in every operation; layout.resize takes split=<id>.

structures.name: The desk (tree host)
structures.does: The one full host of the layout: tile instances, focus, frames, headers, drag, tabs, drawers, zoom, floats, flows drawn. Every key and drag goes through cmd() to an action, and every action's layout change through the screen-layout module.
structures.built: Desk in desk.ts with TILE_ACTIONS; what differs by kind it asks the tile-kind registry. It holds a LayoutState and changes it only by apply (PIE-513): it says what each tile is (facts) and where the person types (layoutCtx), commits the module's answer, and keeps the tile instances, gestures and painting. Its refusal functions are gone into the module. tile.* actions are the one name for each operation; pane.* are their older aliases (PIE-510).

structures.name: Tile kinds
structures.does: What a tile can show: tree, reader, detail, preview, pty, thread, activity, who, art, query (a saved view's cards: a board lane), board, river, brief (its own reader since PIE-515), welcome.list, welcome.detail, welcome.preview, waiting, pinned, backlinks, and any kind an extension registers; and where a container's tiles come from (a tile source: hub:<id>, a hub's views).
structures.built: An open registry (PIE-505): one TileKind entry per kind (make, ^W o keys, actions, default policy, accepts, save, revive, holdsWork, shows, follows, start, describe, view, previewSource). The built-ins register at startup; serviceKind makes an entry whose tile the service draws. Tile sources register the same way (PIE-511: tiles, affects, key); the desk fills columns from them and keeps each tile by its key. The desk never switches on a kind's name. A source says what a tile dropped on its columns does (drop, #105).

questions.text: The tile layer and the protocol import features.

structures.name: Layout descriptions
structures.does: A layout saved by name (daily, river, your own), restored with its tiles, links and ids.
structures.built: Four shapes of one idea: LayoutSpec (desk.json, layouts.json, and the board's layout in delivery.json since PIE-511), SavedDesk, a screen spec's layout (screen-spec.ts, plain data), river.json. The daily agent tile's command comes from EP0CH_DAILY_AGENT when restored.

questions.text: One LayoutSpec shape for river.json too, and presets as screen notes in the outline.

structures.name: State directory
structures.does: Where the door keeps layouts, drafts, marks and its sockets. EP0CH_STATE moves all of it; files are private to the user; two doors on one directory are warned.
structures.built: stateDir, privateDir (the nvim sockets' check, extracted), writeState (temp file and rename), claimState.

structures.name: What's alive in the background
structures.does: A screen that runs programs stays alive when you leave it; D on the menu brings it back.
structures.built: Two owners: App.background and a static Desk.kept.

questions.text: App.background as the one owner.

structures.name: @xterm/headless
structures.does: The terminal emulator inside a tile: full-screen programs draw into it, the door draws its cells.
structures.built: VS Code's emulator, headless, one per terminal tile.

questions.text: No unicode11 addon: emoji are one cell wide and push the row out.

structures.name: nvim
structures.does: The editor in a tile, and ctrl+e's external editor; the door talks to it over its RPC socket (marks as extmarks).
structures.built: Sockets in a private directory, owner-checked; the model the control socket now follows.

structures.name: Herdr
structures.does: The terminal multiplexer the outliner's panes run in. A Herdr pane outlives the door; the door attaches to it.
structures.built: Called through its CLI with a timeout.

structures.name: Terminal tile
structures.does: A program beside the notes: keys go to it while you're in it, ctrl+] leaves, the mouse goes to it when it asked. Its environment says which door and which tile it runs in.
structures.built: PtyPane over a PtyBackend (Bun.Terminal in this process, or a session's terminal host) and @xterm/headless; tileEnv is the one list of what a program doesn't inherit. A terminal's actions belong to its kind (PTY_ACTIONS: tile.type, tile.restart, tile.enter, tile.leave, tile.herdr, #105).

OSC 52 and graphics from a program are dropped.
A terminal tile is named by kind (pty, pty2), not by its program.

structures.name: Herdr agent tile
structures.does: The daily agent runs in a Herdr pane the tile attaches to, so quitting the door leaves it running; the next door reattaches. The App owns that one tile (PIE-498), the first tab of the host layer's drawer (PIE-513): a layout on the one layout engine above every screen, pulled up from the status bar's chip over or beside a screen, as the screen's policy says. No screen has a copy of it.
structures.built: scripts/door-agent-herdr.ts finds or creates the pane under a lock, attaches, and tells the door with tile.herdr over the control socket, as its tile. No title matching.

refs.m: get herdr(): { pane: string; name?: string } | null

questions.text: Reattach shows Herdr's current screen only: no scrollback. In a door session the tile outlives a detach, scrollback and all; a new door still attaches without it.

structures.name: One teardown
structures.does: SIGINT, SIGQUIT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, an uncaught exception or rejection: drafts and ctrl+e text are copied to drafts/, the terminal is put back, the socket removed, and the door says where the text went.
structures.built: guardDoor (door.ts) is the one teardown, for the own terminal and the session alike: every signal and fault calls App.terminate; a small watcher restores the terminal after kill -9. In a door session (door.daemon) a terminal's signals only detach it; the session's own end goes through the same terminate.

questions.text: Six child-process launchers, three with no timeout; unzip blocks the paint.

structures.name: The door session
structures.does: The door keeps running without a terminal (PIE-418): quitting a terminal detaches it, and the screens, layouts, drafts and terminal tiles (programs and scrollback) are there at the next attach. Several terminals at once, the keys wherever the person last typed; ended only by session.end.
structures.built: One daemon per user and state dir runs openDoor on a SessionTerm and serves session.sock beside the control socket; a client probes its terminal, sends input and its size, writes the frames it's sent, runs a program the session hands it. Frames, not state: App renders once and SessionTerm paints each client through its own Painter (size, video mode, Kitty images).

questions.text: Drafts typed since the last put-aside live only in the daemon's memory: a daemon that dies loses them (a handoff puts them aside first).
One session per state dir: a second outline is a second EP0CH_STATE, not a second session in the same one.

structures.name: The terminal host and the restore
structures.does: A terminal tile's program outlives the session's daemon: an upgrade (`ep0ch session upgrade`) or a crash leaves it running, and the next daemon adopts it with its output and reopens the screens and the edits.
structures.built: Bun can't pass a pty between processes, so the ptys live in a host process of their own (pty.sock) behind the PtyBackend seam; PtyPane adopts by its tile (keptAs). The restore is a checkpoint: the screens open as the actions that open them, run again only where the ActionDef declares replay safe, and the edits open on top; each screen's layout is its own saved state.

questions.text: The host's own code can't be upgraded under its programs: a host protocol change ends them, and the tiles start them again.

structures.name: doctor and install
structures.does: Checks and updates the whole stack: facts detected, a plan, then apply.
structures.built: setup/: facts, model, plan, apply, doctor.

questions.text: ~/backups/ep0ch isn't configurable.
Personal infrastructure lives in the door repo.

structures.name: Screen specs
structures.does: A screen as data on the one screen host, the desk: its containers and tiles by kind, a key map naming actions, a hint, a band drawn by a tile kind, where opens land. The desk, the welcome, the brief, Waiting and a pinned page are specs; what each does beyond layout is its tiles' kinds'.
structures.built: ScreenSpec (plain data: specData writes it, readSpec reads it back checked) and the built-in screens registered by name (openScreen). The desk is final: nothing subclasses it. The welcome's list kind is its model and draws its band; the brief's and a pinned page's kinds open beside by policy (opens: beside).

questions.text: Specs stored as notes in the outline (gap 4): the data shape is ready (specData, readSpec, screen.spec).

structures.name: The board
structures.does: Kanban lanes from saved views, a preview and details beside them, the outline and backlinks drawers, floats. Moves and new cards are the service's plans.
structures.built: A screen spec on the desk (PIE-511, PIE-515: boardSpec, plain data): its lanes are query tiles in a columns container filled by the hub source; its drawers, floats, spines, borders, focus and frames are the desk's; its opens land in the readers row (opensInto, keep), a drawer's list closes by shutting its drawer (shuts). What the lanes share is the hub source's model (Lanes): card moves, writes, steps, trash, the hub picker, and lane refresh from the change feed.

questions.text: The spec as a screen note in the outline (gap 4).

structures.name: The river
structures.does: Columns of notes that open to the right; focus moves the keys, not the layout; far columns shrink to peeks and spines.
structures.built: A screen spec on the desk (PIE-515): its columns are river.column tiles (a reader of the note surface with the river's own view: the Library, a note and its replies, a #value branch) in a flow container, the layout engine's squeeze, focus, widen, dock, travel and close; saved to river.json as the desk's layout. Reply counts from one shared index per service.

questions.text: Its filter re-implements query.expression (its palette is retired: the river's g is the desk's search).
A river screen as a note in the outline (gap 4): its spec is plain data (riverSpec).

structures.name: The BBS screens
structures.does: The logon, the main menu, the message lists and reader, Who's Online, Last Callers, Stats, the art viewer, Goodbye: the door as a 1997 BBS.
structures.built: Screen classes in screens.ts. The art screens are compositions and stay as they are; the lists now take actions.

questions.text: Who's Online and Last Callers are built twice (screens and tiles).

structures.name: Screen in a tile
structures.does: A whole screen (the board, the river) inside one tile; the brief is a tile kind of its own since it became a spec (PIE-515).
structures.built: Twice: ScreenTile (board and river only, loaded by require) over the showcase's FramedScreen, and the showcase's own ScreenPane. The desk imports the showcase.

questions.text: One ScreenTile over a screen registry; delete ScreenPane.

structures.name: Searches
structures.does: Find a note: the desk's / (the river's g), the board's picker. The BBS Search screen, never constructed, is gone (PIE-510).
structures.built: Separate implementations over different sources; none uses tree.search.

questions.text: One jump palette as a shell overlay over tree.search.

structures.name: WoE art packs
structures.does: Shypht's 1997 ANSI art: the logon, the menu, the logos. Read in place from the packs, never copied.
structures.built: packs.ts opens the zips; ansi.ts is an ANSI.SYS-style interpreter (CP437 in, VGA cells out). A glyph CP437 lacks is sent as its nearest one (CP437_NEAREST, #103).

questions.text: PACK_DIR defaults to a path on one machine.

structures.name: Control socket
structures.does: The door's own socket: peek, snap, open, actions, act, subscribe. Agents, tile programs and the Herdr wrapper all come through it. It is the door's shell, so it is private.
structures.built: startControl sweeps dead sockets, listens in a folder that is the user's alone, chmods 0600, caps request lines; snap writes only under the state dir; the feed disconnects a subscriber that stops reading.

questions.text: The feed says what changed on screen, never which action ran or who ran it.

structures.name: act, peek and the live feed
structures.does: An agent sees what the person sees and does what they do. Its action is named on the status bar, recorded as author agent with its actor id, and never takes the person's focus, selection or keys.
structures.built: App.act runs the request through the App's dispatcher (the host layer's, the shell's and the extensions' sets, then the screen's own dispatcher); App.subscribe diffs each screen's viewState after a paint.

questions.text: `open` is three actions with different arguments; `pin` is four things.
Each screen hand-routes act and names its readers its own way (resolved: one dispatcher, one tile= grammar).

structures.name: Attention marks
structures.does: block.mark: a block framed and labelled in every tile showing it, an extmark in nvim. How an agent points the person at something.
structures.built: LocalMarks in marks.json, re-read before each change so two doors don't lose each other's.

questions.text: Marks belong in the service (marks.* and feed events), so Detail, Tree and agents see them.

structures.name: ep0ch act | peek | snap
structures.does: The command line an agent uses: `ep0ch act card.move lane=Doing --as <id>`, `ep0ch peek`, `ep0ch subscribe`.
structures.built: main.ts's subcommands write one request line to the control socket (EP0CH_CONTROL) and print the answer.

structures.name: Outliner CLI
structures.does: list, create, update and the rest for scripts and agents, with author and actor on every write; door-open shows a block in the door.
structures.built: cli.ts over the outliner client; door-open goes to the door's control socket.

structures.name: Claude mod
structures.does: Outliner tools inside Claude Code; `show` opens a note in the door from Claude's own tile, where that tile's opens land.
structures.built: register.ts registers the tools; door-open --from $EP0CH_TILE.

structures.name: Extensions
structures.does: Folders of trusted code the service runs, in four kinds: data records (moon::, jira::), inline output (horoscope::), rich components from shared primitives (fancy-horror::) and tile kinds (tarot.reading), plus @name agents addressed while writing. Added or removed without a restart; everything they write is ext:<id>.
structures.built: ExtensionRegistry watches the outline's extensions/ and the user folder, builds a candidate registry from every extension.json and publishes it in one step (extensions.list, a change-feed event). Each call is a fresh process (ExtensionCalls; runCommand passes only PATH and LANG, caps output and kills the process group). AgentRequests runs @name lines once the note is quiet. Contract 1 manifests are still read for the legacy registry.

questions.text: Credential lookup is macOS-only (keychain); on Linux a keychain credential is unavailable.

structures.name: Component renderers
structures.does: component: fences drawn from a renderer registry (labelled values, one layout so far), in Detail and the door.
structures.built: document-components.ts reads the registry from the host's config.

questions.text: The door mirrors the registry from its own machine's config; for a remote door the service should render.

structures.name: Extensions in the door
structures.does: The door binds what the service's extensions offer: handler lines drawn under their line (records, output, components from the shared primitives), each action an ActionDef (ext.<id>.<action>: its key, a click on its control, act), and each extension tile kind registered as a program tile. Any program in a terminal tile can still drive its door over EP0CH_CONTROL as EP0CH_TILE; the Claude mod and the Herdr agent do.
structures.built: src/extensions.ts reads extensions.list and binds again when the feed says it changed: EXT_ACTIONS for lines and blocks, serviceKind for tile kinds. tileEnv gives a tile's program its door and its tile.

questions.text: A screen still can't add a key or a mouse spot without editing its keyIn; an extension's line actions can.

structures.name: pi extension
structures.does: The outliner inside pi: /outliner, /outliner-task, /capture, and the delivery lifecycle.
structures.built: pi-extension/index.ts registers commands and renderers.

structures.name: Publisher
structures.does: Serves blocks marked [publish::…] read-only at a URL; an attached .html or .md file as the page. This map is published through it.
structures.built: A client of the service: blocks.query finds published blocks, the content feed drops its cache. Attachments only from allowed roots; attached HTML runs in a CSP sandbox without allow-same-origin.

iso.about: Where the blocks stand: scripts/architecture-map/iso.ts places them by lane and dependency depth; place sets a cell by hand, [column, row inside the lane].

trace.title: m moves a card
trace.about: The path the code takes today when the person presses m on a board card and picks a lane. m only opens the mover, an input state; the move itself is card.move, the same ActionDef that H, L, a drag and an agent's act run (PIE-506 closed the gap PIE-492 named).

steps.label: key m
steps.what: The lanes' key handler opens the mover: an input state that holds the keys, and changes nothing until it ends.

steps.label: mover asks
steps.what: openMover asks the service for every lane's plan at once, at the card's revision.

steps.label: views.planWrite
steps.what: SocketBoard sends one views.planWrite request over the service socket.

steps.label: plan
steps.what: The service splits each lane's query and plans the property patch, or refuses with the reason.

steps.label: enter
steps.what: The mover shows each lane's plan; Enter checks the selection hasn't changed and runs the card.move action, which calls moveTo.

steps.label: properties.patch
steps.what: moveTo re-plans the target lane, then applyMove sends properties.patch with expectedRevision and the actor's provenance.

steps.label: revision check
steps.what: The store refuses if the card changed since it was read; otherwise it patches the tokens and writes the text.

steps.label: change feed
steps.what: The change is recorded in the feed and broadcast as an event to every subscriber: this door, other doors, Detail, Tree, the publisher.

steps.label: event in
steps.what: Each door's SocketBoard hands the event to App.event, which passes it to the screen on top.

steps.label: which lanes
steps.what: The board works out which lanes the change touches (asking planWrite which lanes the card is 'already' in) and marks them.

steps.label: lanes repaint
steps.what: Each marked lane, a query tile in the board's columns container, reads its view again with views.read and draws. In the door that moved it, moveTo's finally reloads the source and target lanes.
